cards.k: About 73,000 Years Ago · 大約七萬三千年前
cards.en: The oldest drawing we know of
cards.body_en: In 2018 researchers reported a cross-hatched pattern drawn with an ochre crayon on a flake of stone. It came from layers about 73,000 years old in Blombos Cave, South Africa. Drawings that show things or patterns were known before this find only from the last 40,000 years. The stone carries a few crossing lines and no picture of anything. Lines came first.
cards.body_zh: 2018 年，研究者發表了一件用赭石「蠟筆」畫在石片上的交叉線圖案，出自南非布隆伯斯洞穴大約七萬三千年前的地層。在這之前，已知的繪畫（不論畫的是東西還是圖案）都只有四萬年以內的。這片石頭上只有幾條交叉的線，沒有畫出任何東西。最先出現的，是線。

cards.body_en: Taiwan's Ministry of Education dictionary defines baimiao as a way of painting that draws things with lines alone and adds no color, used mostly for figures and flowers. An education encyclopedia adds that a skilled painter can show solid form, movement, and texture through the thickness, firmness, curve, and spacing of the lines. Chinese painting and calligraphy also share the same tools: brush and ink.
cards.body_zh: 教育部辭典對「白描」的解釋是：「一種畫法。僅用線條勾描物象，而不著以顏色，多用於人物和花卉的繪畫上。」《教育大辭書》補充：純熟的白描技法，可以藉線條的粗細、剛柔、曲直、疏密等，表現形體的立體感、動態感和質感。國畫和書法用的也是同樣的工具：筆和墨。

cards.body_en: Sometimes a brushstroke has streaks where no ink reached the paper. The Ministry of Education dictionary describes a style of writing named for this look, flying white: strokes with empty, inkless places, as if written with a dry brush. A legend says the Han-dynasty scholar Cai Yong got the idea from watching workmen write with a whitewash broom. The gaps in this page's fast line imitate that look.
cards.body_zh: 有時候一筆畫裡會有幾絲沒沾到墨的空白。教育部辭典記載了一種以此得名的書體「飛白書」：「筆畫中有空白無墨之處，絲絲露白，有如枯筆寫成的模樣。」相傳東漢的蔡邕看見工匠用刷粉的帚寫字，而得到啟發。這一頁那條「很快的線」上的空隙，模仿的就是這種樣子。

cards.body_en: Paul Klee taught at the Bauhaus school in Germany. His Pedagogical Sketchbook, published in 1925, begins: “An active line on a walk, moving freely, without goal. A walk for a walk's sake.” The mover, he wrote, is a point that shifts its position forward. The well-known sayings about taking a line for a walk are shortened versions of this opening.
cards.body_zh: 保羅・克利曾在德國的包浩斯學校教書。他 1925 年出版的《教學筆記》（Pedagogical Sketchbook）這樣開頭：「一條主動的線在散步，自由地移動，沒有目的地。為散步而散步。」他寫道，推動這條線的，是一個不斷往前移動的點。大家熟悉的「帶一條線去散步」，是這段開頭的簡化說法。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The visual arts curriculum names points, lines, and planes directly for grades 3 and 4. The other entries are the closest ones, and their links to this lesson are our reading of them.
curric.lead_zh: 視覺藝術課綱在國小三、四年級直接點名了「點線面」。其他幾條是最接近的條目；它們和這一課的連結，是本教材的解讀。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 點線面創作體驗、平面與立體創作、聯想創作。
items.note_en: This lesson is about the line, from the point that moves to the shape a line closes.
items.note_zh: 這一課講的就是線：從一個移動的點，到線圍成的面。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 媒材、技法及工具知能。
items.note_en: Pencil, marker, and brush each make a different line, and hatching is a technique.
items.note_zh: 鉛筆、粗筆和毛筆各畫出不同的線；細線法是一種技法。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 視覺元素、生活之美、視覺聯想。
items.note_en: Line is one of the visual elements, and reading a line's speed and weight is a kind of visual association.
items.note_zh: 線是視覺元素之一；從一條線讀出快慢與輕重，是一種視覺聯想。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 視覺元素、色彩與構成要素的辨識與溝通。
items.note_en: Words such as outline, contour, and hatching let students say what they see.
items.note_zh: 外框線、輪廓線、細線法這些詞，讓學生能說出自己看到的。

myths.myth_en: A line only shows where the edge of a thing is.
myths.myth_zh: 線只是用來標出東西的邊緣。
myths.fact_en: A line also shows how it was made. Its width, its edge, and its gaps record the pressure, the steadiness, and the speed of the hand, and close-set lines can even make shading.
myths.fact_zh: 線也讓人看出它是怎麼畫的：粗細、邊緣和空隙，記錄了下筆的力道、手穩不穩和速度；排得很密的線甚至可以畫出明暗。

myths.myth_en: Horizontal lines always feel calm and diagonal lines always feel exciting.
myths.myth_zh: 水平線一定讓人平靜，斜線一定讓人興奮。
myths.fact_en: Museum teaching pages say horizontal lines suggest rest and diagonal lines can give a feeling of movement. Those are common habits of seeing that artists use. They are not laws, and one picture can use the same kind of line in another way.
myths.fact_zh: 博物館的教學資料寫的是：水平線「讓人聯想到」休息，斜線「可以」帶來動的感覺。這些是常見的觀看習慣，藝術家會運用它們；但它們不是定律，同一種線在別的圖裡可以有別的用法。

myths.myth_en: Paul Klee wrote, “A line is a dot that went for a walk.”
myths.myth_zh: 保羅・克利寫過：「線是一個去散步的點。」
myths.fact_en: That is a popular short version. His book of 1925 begins, “An active line on a walk, moving freely, without goal,” and goes on to say that the mover is a point shifting its position forward.
myths.fact_zh: 那是流行的簡化版。他 1925 年的書開頭寫的是「一條主動的線在散步，自由地移動，沒有目的地」，接著才說推動它的是一個不斷往前移動的點。

myths.myth_en: A good line is perfectly smooth and the same width all the way.
myths.myth_zh: 好的線條，就是從頭到尾一樣粗、完全平滑。
myths.fact_en: An even line is one choice among many. Artists change a line from thick to thin, hard to soft, and dark to light on purpose, and in baimiao those changes are what show weight and movement.
myths.fact_zh: 均勻的線只是眾多選擇之一。藝術家會刻意讓線由粗變細、由硬變軟、由深變淺；在白描裡，正是這些變化表現出重量和動態。

tricks.title_en: A line is a point that moved
tricks.body_en: Every line is the path of something that traveled.
tricks.body_zh: 每一條線，都是某個東西走過的路。

tricks.body_en: Press harder for a thicker line, and lift for a thinner one.
tricks.body_zh: 壓重一點線就粗，提起來線就細。

tricks.title_zh: 平的像休息，斜的像在動
tricks.body_en: Horizontal lines suggest rest and diagonals suggest movement. These are suggestions, not rules.
tricks.body_zh: 水平線讓人聯想到休息，斜線讓人聯想到動。這是聯想，不是規則。

tricks.body_en: Close parallel lines are hatching, and crossed ones are cross-hatching.
tricks.body_zh: 排得很密的平行線是細線法；交叉起來就是交叉線法。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: Carry pencils and brushes with the point down, and do not walk around with one in your mouth.
safety.zh: 拿著鉛筆或毛筆走動時，筆尖朝下；不要把筆含在嘴裡走路。

safety.en: Cover the desk before you use ink or markers, and keep ink away from books and screens. Wash brushes and hands when you finish.
safety.zh: 用墨汁或粗筆之前先把桌面鋪好，墨汁要離書本和螢幕遠一點。畫完把筆和手洗乾淨。

safety.en: Put the caps back on markers. Use markers made for school, and open a window if the smell is strong.
safety.zh: 粗筆用完要蓋回筆蓋。請用學校用的筆；味道太重就打開窗戶。

safety.en: Rest your eyes when you draw on a screen: ten minutes after every thirty minutes of close work.
safety.zh: 在螢幕上畫圖也要讓眼睛休息：用眼每 30 分鐘休息 10 分鐘。

materials.en: A soft pencil and white paper
materials.zh: 一支軟的鉛筆和白紙

materials.en: A brush with ink or dark watercolor, and paper that can take water
materials.zh: 一支毛筆，加上墨汁或深色水彩，以及吸水的紙

materials.en: A watch or a timer
materials.zh: 手錶或計時器

materials.en: This page, with the five lines on the left
materials.zh: 這一頁，左邊的五種線

steps.en: Watch the five lines on the page. For each one, write down two words that describe it.
steps.zh: 看頁面上的五種線。每一種各寫下兩個形容它的詞。

steps.en: With the pencil, draw the same wavy line five ways: light and steady, heavy, as fast as you can, with a shaky hand, and from heavy to light.
steps.zh: 用鉛筆把同一條波浪線畫五次：輕而穩、重、盡量快、手抖著畫、由重到輕。

steps.en: Do the same with the brush. Time the slow line and the fast line.
steps.zh: 用毛筆再畫一次這五種線。替慢的那一條和快的那一條計時。

steps.en: Look at your fast brush line. Does it have gaps? Load the brush with more ink and try again. Then try with less.
steps.zh: 看看你用毛筆很快畫的那一條：上面有空隙嗎？讓筆多沾一點墨再畫一次；然後少沾一點再畫一次。

steps.en: Compare your ten lines with the five on the screen. Where does the model match your paper, and where does it not?
steps.zh: 把你的十條線和螢幕上的五條比一比。模型和紙上的結果，哪裡一樣？哪裡不一樣？

activities.tip_en: On this page a fast stroke always leaves gaps. On paper you may find that a brush full of ink leaves none however fast you go, and a nearly dry brush leaves them even when you go slowly. That difference is worth writing down.
activities.tip_zh: 在這一頁，畫得快就一定有空隙。在紙上你可能會發現：吸飽墨的筆不管畫多快都沒有空隙，而快乾掉的筆就算慢慢畫也有。這個差別值得記下來。

activities.title_en: Shade a Ball with Lines Only
activities.title_zh: 只用線條替一顆球畫上明暗

materials.en: A sharp pencil or a fine pen, and white paper
materials.zh: 一支削尖的鉛筆或細字筆，和白紙

materials.en: A ruler
materials.zh: 一把尺

materials.en: Lesson 3 of this series, open at the model of the ball
materials.zh: 本系列第三課，停在那顆球的模型

steps.en: Draw a row of four boxes. Leave the first one empty.
steps.zh: 畫一排四個格子，第一格留白。

steps.en: Fill the second box with thin parallel lines set far apart, and the third with lines set close together.
steps.zh: 第二格畫上細細的平行線，排得疏一點；第三格的線排得密一點。

steps.en: In the fourth box, draw close lines and then cross them with a second set. You now have four values made of lines alone.
steps.zh: 第四格先畫密密的線，再用另一組線和它交叉。現在你有四階只用線條做出來的明度。

steps.en: Draw a circle. Use your four boxes as a guide to shade it like the ball in Lesson 3, with no smudging: open paper toward the light, crossed lines in the darkest band.
steps.zh: 畫一個圓。照著這四格，替它畫上像第三課那顆球的明暗，不要用手抹：朝著光的地方留白，最暗的那一圈用交叉的線。

steps.en: Hold the drawing at arm's length. Do the lines blend into gray? Step back until they do, and measure how far that is.
steps.zh: 把畫拿到一隻手臂遠的地方看。線條有沒有融成一片灰？一直往後退，退到融成灰為止，量量看那是多遠。

activities.tip_en: Keep the lines in each box the same weight and change only how close they are. If your hatching follows the curve of the ball, the ball will look rounder. Try it both ways and compare.
activities.tip_zh: 同一格裡的線要一樣粗，只改變它們的疏密。如果你的線順著球面彎，球看起來會更圓。兩種畫法都試試，再比較。

links_head.zh: 書法裡的線、畫明暗的線，以及下一課

links.zh: 一枝毛筆怎麼寫出粗細？
links.note_en: Pressing down and lifting up with a real brush, shown in slow motion. The brush on this page borrows the idea.
links.note_zh: 用真的毛筆下壓和提起，放慢來看。這一頁的毛筆借用的就是這個道理。

links.en: How Does Shading Make a Circle Look Like a Ball?
links.zh: 明暗怎麼把圓形變成球？
links.note_en: An outline alone gives a flat circle. Hatching is one way to add the light and shade that make it round.
links.note_zh: 只有輪廓，就只是一個平面的圓。細線法是替它加上明暗、讓它變圓的一種方法。

links.zh: 怎麼在平面上畫出一個房間？

links.note_zh: 單元二從一組往同一個點靠攏的線開始，還有一條可以讓眼睛走進去的走廊。

units.blurb_en: How a flat sheet of paper can hold a room, a mountain range, or a face, and where to put the main thing.
units.blurb_zh: 一張平平的紙，怎麼裝得下一個房間、一片山脈或一張臉；主角又該放在哪裡。

lessons.title: How Do You Draw a Room on Flat Paper?
lessons.title_zh: 怎麼在平面上畫出一個房間？
lessons.blurb_en: Look down a hallway through a window and move your eye up, down, and sideways. Watch the vanishing point follow you, then find it yourself in five line drawings.
lessons.blurb_zh: 透過一扇窗戶看一條走廊，把眼睛往上、往下、往旁邊移動，看消失點怎麼跟著你走；再到五張線稿裡自己把它找出來。
lessons.big_idea_en: Lines that are parallel and run away from you look as if they meet at one point, the vanishing point. That point sits on a level line at the height of your eyes, the eye-level line. Things of the same size are drawn smaller the farther away they are. With those three ideas you can draw a room on a flat sheet of paper.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 彼此平行、而且離你越來越遠的線，看起來會在一個點相交，那就是消失點。消失點落在一條和眼睛一樣高的水平線上，叫做視平線。一樣大的東西，離得越遠就畫得越小。有了這三件事，就能在一張平平的紙上畫出一個房間。

lab.title_en: A Hallway Seen Through a Window
lab.how_en: Imagine a window 4 meters wide and 3 meters tall standing at the mouth of a hallway. Your eye is 3 meters in front of it. Drag the picture, or use the sliders, to move your eye. The window never moves. The dotted line marks your eye level and the gold dot marks the vanishing point. Switch to Line drawing to see the same view as lines on paper, and turn on the two posts to compare near and far.
lab.how_zh: 想像走廊口立著一扇寬 4 公尺、高 3 公尺的窗戶，你的眼睛在窗戶前面 3 公尺的地方。拖動畫面或用滑桿，移動的是你的眼睛；窗戶不會動。點狀的線標出視平線，金色的圓點標出消失點。切換到「紙上的線稿」，看同一個畫面變成紙上的線；打開兩根柱子，比較近和遠。

legend.en: The gold dot: the vanishing point, straight in front of your eye
legend.zh: 金色圓點：消失點，就在眼睛的正前方

legend.en: The dotted line: the eye-level line (the horizon line of the picture)
legend.zh: 點狀的線：視平線（這張畫的地平線）

legend.en: The dashed gold lines: the edges of the hallway, continued to the vanishing point
legend.zh: 金色虛線：走廊的邊線，一路延長到消失點

lab.scale_en: The hallway is 4 m wide, 3 m tall, and 18 m long, with floor tiles 1 m square. The three eye heights (0.6 m, 1.2 m, 2.2 m) are round numbers chosen for the model.
lab.scale_zh: 走廊寬 4 公尺、高 3 公尺、長 18 公尺，地磚每塊 1 公尺見方。三種眼睛高度（0.6、1.2、2.2 公尺）是替模型選的整數，不是量出來的。

notes.en: The model uses one eye that stays still. You have two eyes, and they are always moving. Linear perspective is a system for drawing from a single fixed viewpoint. It is close to what we see, and it is not the same thing.
notes.zh: 模型用的是一隻不動的眼睛。你有兩隻眼睛，而且它們一直在動。線性透視是一套「從單一固定視點來畫」的方法；它很接近我們看到的樣子，但不等於視覺本身。

notes.en: Every line going into the distance here is level and points straight ahead, so there is one vanishing point. Turn a box at an angle and it needs two. Lines that slope up or down, such as a roof or a ramp, meet above or below the eye-level line.
notes.zh: 這裡每一條往遠處延伸的線都是水平的，而且朝正前方，所以只有一個消失點。把一個箱子轉個角度，就需要兩個。往上或往下斜的線（例如屋頂、斜坡），則在視平線的上方或下方相交。

notes.en: A perspective picture is exactly right from one spot only: the place where the eye was. From anywhere else it is a little off, though it usually still looks fine.
notes.zh: 一張透視圖，只有從一個位置看才完全正確：就是當初眼睛所在的地方。從別的地方看都有一點偏差，不過通常看起來還是可以。

notes.en: The walls and floor are flat colors with no light and shade. Lesson 3 showed what shading adds, and Lesson 6 looks at other ways painters show distance.
notes.zh: 牆和地板都是平塗的顏色，沒有明暗。明暗能加上什麼，第三課講過了；畫家表現遠近的其他方法，留到第六課。

lab.note_end_en: So test it in a real hallway. Classroom Activity 1 shows how, with nothing more than a window pane and a marker.
lab.note_end_zh: 所以請到真的走廊去驗證；做法在課堂活動一，只需要一片透明的板子和一支筆。

paras: Look at a photograph of a straight railway track, or stand at one end of a long hallway at school. The two sides are the same distance apart all the way along. You know that. Yet they look as if they are closing in on each other, and far away they seem to touch. Your paper is flat, and a room is not. The trick of drawing a room is to copy this closing-in exactly.

Artists call the system linear perspective. Its first rule is about parallel lines. Lines that run away from you, side by side, look as if they meet at a single point. That point is called the vanishing point. The sides of a road and the rails of a railway are the examples everyone knows. In a hallway the edges of the floor and the ceiling do the same thing, and so do the tops of the doors.

Where is the vanishing point? It is on a level line at the height of your own eyes. Artists call it the eye-level line or the horizon line. Crouch down and it drops. Climb on a chair and it rises with you. Things below your eye level, like the floor, have lines that slope up toward it. Things above your eye level, like the ceiling, have lines that slope down. Step to the left and the vanishing point moves left as well. It is always straight in front of you.

The second rule is about size. Things look smaller the farther away they are. Move a post twice as far from your eye and it looks half as tall. Move it three times as far and it looks one third as tall. The post has not changed. It simply takes up a smaller angle in your view. Perspective lets a painter work out exactly how big to draw each thing for its distance.

People in Florence, Italy, worked this system out about six hundred years ago. It is generally accepted that the architect Filippo Brunelleschi made a series of experiments between 1415 and 1420, drawing the city's buildings in correct perspective. His painted panels are lost. In 1435 Leon Battista Alberti wrote the method down in a book called On Painting. A few years earlier the painter Masaccio had already used it for a wall painting of the Trinity in a church in Florence.

Linear perspective is one way of drawing space. It is not the only way. It assumes one eye that never moves, while you have two eyes that are always moving. Chinese landscape painters chose a different path. Their pictures do not keep to a single fixed viewpoint, and the eye travels through them as if on a walk. Lesson 15 goes there. For now, find the eye level, find the vanishing point, and aim your lines at it.
paras_zh: 看一張筆直鐵軌的照片，或站在學校長長的走廊的一頭。兩邊之間的距離，從頭到尾都一樣寬，這你是知道的。可是它們看起來卻越靠越近，到了很遠的地方好像碰在一起。紙是平的，房間不是。要畫出一個房間，訣竅就是把這種「越靠越近」原原本本地畫下來。
藝術家把這套方法叫做線性透視。第一條規則和平行線有關：並排著、離你越來越遠的線，看起來會在同一個點相交。這個點叫做消失點。馬路的兩邊和鐵路的兩條軌道，是大家都知道的例子。在走廊裡，地板和天花板的邊線也是這樣，每一扇門的上緣也是。
消失點在哪裡？在一條和你的眼睛一樣高的水平線上。藝術家把這條線叫做視平線，也叫地平線。蹲下來，它就降低；站到椅子上，它跟著你升高。比視平線低的東西，例如地板，它的線往上斜向視平線；比視平線高的東西，例如天花板，它的線往下斜。往左跨一步，消失點也跟著往左。它永遠在你的正前方。
第二條規則和大小有關：東西離得越遠，看起來越小。把一根柱子移到離眼睛兩倍遠的地方，它看起來只有一半高；三倍遠，就只有三分之一高。柱子並沒有變，只是它在你視野裡占的角度變小了。有了透視，畫家就能算出每一樣東西在那個距離該畫多大。
大約六百年前，義大利佛羅倫斯的人把這套方法弄清楚了。一般認為，建築師布魯內萊斯基在 1415 到 1420 年之間做了一連串實驗，用正確的透視畫出城裡的建築。他畫的那幾塊板子已經失傳。1435 年，阿爾伯蒂把這個方法寫進一本叫《論繪畫》的書。在這之前幾年，畫家馬薩喬已經用它在佛羅倫斯的一座教堂裡畫了〈聖三位一體〉壁畫。
線性透視是畫出空間的一種方法，不是唯一的方法。它假設只有一隻不動的眼睛，而你有兩隻一直在動的眼睛。中國的山水畫家走的是另一條路：他們的畫不拘泥於單一固定的視點，眼睛可以在畫裡像散步一樣移動。那是第十五課的事。現在，先找出視平線，找出消失點，再讓你的線對準它。
questions: You are drawing a hallway. Where on your paper should the vanishing point go, and what decides it?
Two posts are the same height. One is 5 m from your eye and the other is 15 m away. How do their heights compare on your drawing?
Why is a perspective drawing not exactly the same as what a person sees?
answers: It goes on the eye-level line, straight in front of where your eye is. If you are low, the line is low on the paper. If you stand to one side, the point moves to that side.
The far post is three times as far away, so it is drawn one third as tall as the near one.
Linear perspective assumes one eye that stays in one place. People look with two eyes that keep moving. The drawing is a close and very useful approximation.

vocab.ex: The vanishing point is at your eye level.

vocab.ex: The sun went down below the horizon.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Your eye rises from 0.6 m to 2.2 m. The eye-level line and the vanishing point rise with it the whole way.
parts.text_zh: 眼睛從 0.6 公尺升到 2.2 公尺。視平線和消失點一路跟著升高。

parts.text_en: You walk from the left wall to the right. The vanishing point crosses the picture with you, always straight ahead.
parts.text_zh: 你從左邊的牆走到右邊。消失點跟著你橫越畫面，永遠在正前方。

parts.text_en: The same view becomes black lines on paper. Follow any edge that goes into the distance and it leads to the gold dot.
parts.text_zh: 同一個畫面變成紙上的黑線。順著任何一條往遠處去的邊線走，都會走到金色的圓點。

parts.zh: 一樣高，畫出來不一樣大
parts.text_en: Two posts of equal height stand near and far. The far one is three times as far away and one third as tall on the picture.
parts.text_zh: 兩根一樣高的柱子，一近一遠。遠的那一根是三倍遠，在畫面上只有三分之一高。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Where must your eye be for the floor to fill most of the picture? Can you put the vanishing point exactly on the handle of the door at the far end?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。眼睛要在哪裡，地板才會占掉大半個畫面？你能把消失點剛好放在盡頭那扇門的門把上嗎？

vp.lead_en: Five line drawings: hallways, railway tracks, and a street. In each one, click the spot where the lines that go into the distance would meet. You can move your mark with the arrow buttons. Press Check to see how close you were. The drawing then continues its own lines to the true point.
vp.lead_zh: 五張線稿：走廊、鐵軌和一條街。每一張都點出那些往遠處延伸的線會相交的地方；可以用方向按鈕移動你標的位置。按「對答案」看看差多少，圖上會把它自己的線一路延長到真正的消失點。
vp.note_en: A tip from drawing class: lay a ruler along two of the receding lines, one after the other, and see where they cross.
vp.note_zh: 素描課的小技巧：拿一把尺，先後貼著兩條往遠處去的線，看它們在哪裡交叉。

posts.lead_en: Two posts stand in the hallway. Slide post B nearer or farther and read the numbers. In the room the two posts are always the same height. On the picture they are not. Then draw the lines through their tops and their feet, and see where those lines go.
posts.lead_zh: 走廊裡立著兩根柱子。把柱子 B 滑近或滑遠，讀讀數字。在走廊裡，兩根柱子永遠一樣高；在畫面上卻不是。再畫出通過頂端和底端的線，看看這些線通到哪裡。
posts.note_en: This is the rule from the reading: an object looks N times smaller when it is N times as far from the eye.
posts.note_zh: 這就是課文裡的規則：一樣東西離眼睛 N 倍遠，看起來就是 N 分之一大。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Vanishing Point · 消失點背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A lost panel, a book, a wall in Florence, and mountains seen while walking
culture_cards.title_zh: 一塊失傳的板子、一本書、佛羅倫斯的一面牆，和邊走邊看的山
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people learned to put space on a flat surface.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人怎麼把空間放到平面上的四個小故事。

cards.k: Florence, about 1415–1420 · 佛羅倫斯，約 1415–1420 年
cards.zh: 布魯內萊斯基失傳的板子
cards.body_en: Filippo Brunelleschi was an architect. The Metropolitan Museum's timeline says he demonstrated his system of linear perspective in two experimental panels showing buildings in Florence, the Baptistery and the Palazzo della Signoria. Both panels are lost. Later writers reported that, in about 1420, he had people look at a painted panel through a small hole. Because the panels are gone, nobody can check today how exact they were.
cards.body_zh: 布魯內萊斯基是一位建築師。大都會博物館的年表說，他用兩塊實驗用的板子示範了線性透視，畫的是佛羅倫斯的洗禮堂和領主宮。兩塊板子都已經失傳。後來的作者記載，大約在 1420 年，他讓人透過一個小孔去看畫好的板子。板子不在了，所以今天沒有人能檢查它們到底有多準。

cards.body_en: Leon Battista Alberti wrote On Painting in Latin in 1435, and an Italian version followed in 1436, addressed to Brunelleschi. The National Gallery in London says the single-point system was invented by Brunelleschi and set out by Alberti in this book. Its glossary describes the picture plane as a transparent division between the space inside the painting and the real space where the viewer stands. The window in this lesson's model is that idea.
cards.body_zh: 阿爾伯蒂在 1435 年用拉丁文寫了《論繪畫》，1436 年又有義大利文版，書前的獻詞是寫給布魯內萊斯基的。倫敦國家美術館說，單點透視由布魯內萊斯基發明，由阿爾伯蒂在這本書裡整理成文。它的詞彙表把「畫面」形容成一道透明的分界：一邊是畫裡的空間，一邊是觀看的人所站的真實空間。這一課模型裡的那扇窗戶，就是這個想法。

cards.body_en: In the church of Santa Maria Novella in Florence, Masaccio painted the Trinity on a flat wall so that it looks like a deep chapel with a curved ceiling. The Met's timeline says it applies Brunelleschi's ideas of linear perspective to painting, and the vanishing point is at the viewer's eye level. It is an early and famous example. It is not perfect: studies of its geometry have found errors, as in most paintings of that century.
cards.body_zh: 在佛羅倫斯的新聖母教堂，馬薩喬在一面平平的牆上畫了〈聖三位一體〉，看起來卻像一間有拱頂的深深的小禮拜堂。大都會博物館的年表說，這件作品把布魯內萊斯基的線性透視用到了繪畫上；它的消失點就在觀看者眼睛的高度。這是早期很有名的例子，但並不完美：研究它的幾何的人發現了誤差，那個世紀的大多數畫作也是如此。

cards.body_en: Taiwan's Ministry of Education dictionary says that Chinese painting commonly arranges its scenes with a moving viewpoint and does not keep to a single focus point of perspective. An education encyclopedia adds that Chinese landscapes use many points where Western landscapes use one, so one picture can show height, depth, and level distance together. It is a different answer to the same question, and Lesson 15 returns to it.
cards.body_zh: 教育部辭典說，中國畫「普遍以移動視點的方式取景布局，視野寬廣，不拘泥於焦點透視」。《教育大辭書》補充：中國山水畫不像西洋風景畫採單點透視，而採多點透視或散點透視，所以一個畫面裡往往同時有高遠、深遠、平遠三種空間。這是對同一個問題的另一種回答；第十五課會再回來談。

curric.lead_en: The visual arts curriculum does not use the word perspective. These are the closest entries, and their links to this lesson are our reading of them.
curric.lead_zh: 視覺藝術課綱的條文沒有出現「透視」。下面是最接近的條目；它們和這一課的連結，是本教材的解讀。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 色彩感知、造形與空間的探索。
items.note_en: Exploring space is the subject of this unit, and perspective is one way to draw it.
items.note_zh: 「空間的探索」正是這個單元的主題；透視是畫出空間的一種方法。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 點線面創作體驗、平面與立體創作、聯想創作。
items.note_en: A point, lines aimed at it, and the planes between them: a room in perspective is built from exactly these.
items.note_zh: 一個點、對準它的線、線與線之間的面：透視裡的房間就是用這些組成的。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國中）
items.text: 平面、立體及複合媒材的表現技法。
items.note_en: Linear perspective is a technique for showing a solid space on a flat surface.
items.note_zh: 線性透視是在平面上表現立體空間的一種技法。

items.area: 自然科學領域（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 光線以直線前進，反射時有一定的方向。
items.note_en: The model works because light travels in straight lines from each point of the hallway to the eye.
items.note_zh: 模型之所以成立，是因為光從走廊的每一點沿直線走到眼睛。

myths.myth_en: The vanishing point is always in the middle of the paper.
myths.myth_zh: 消失點一定在紙的正中間。
myths.fact_en: It is straight in front of the eye, at eye level. If the viewer is low, high, or off to one side, the point moves there. In the model you can put it almost anywhere.
myths.fact_zh: 消失點在眼睛的正前方、和眼睛一樣高的地方。觀看的人位置偏低、偏高或偏向一邊，它就跟著移過去。在模型裡，你幾乎可以把它放在任何地方。

myths.myth_en: Things far away are drawn smaller because they really are smaller.
myths.myth_zh: 遠處的東西畫得比較小，是因為它們真的比較小。
myths.fact_en: Their size has not changed. A thing that is farther away takes up a smaller angle in your view, so it is drawn smaller. Two posts of the same height prove it.
myths.fact_zh: 它們的大小並沒有變。東西離得遠，在視野裡占的角度就小，所以畫得小。兩根一樣高的柱子就能證明這件事。

myths.myth_en: Linear perspective shows the world exactly as our eyes see it.
myths.myth_zh: 線性透視畫出來的，就是眼睛看到的樣子。
myths.fact_en: It is a geometric system for one eye that does not move. We see with two eyes in constant motion. The picture is an approximation, and it is exactly right from one viewing spot only.
myths.fact_zh: 它是替「一隻不動的眼睛」設計的幾何方法。我們是用兩隻不停移動的眼睛在看。畫出來的是近似，而且只有從一個觀看位置看才完全正確。

myths.myth_en: A picture without a vanishing point is drawn wrong.
myths.myth_zh: 沒有消失點的畫，就是畫錯了。
myths.fact_en: Linear perspective is one way of showing space. Chinese landscape painting uses a moving viewpoint, and painters in the Netherlands made convincing rooms by eye, without the Italian system.
myths.fact_zh: 線性透視是表現空間的一種方法。中國山水畫用的是移動的視點；尼德蘭的畫家不靠義大利那套方法，憑觀察也畫出了令人信服的房間。

tricks.body_en: Parallel lines that run away from you aim at one vanishing point.
tricks.body_zh: 離你遠去的平行線，都對準同一個消失點。

tricks.title_zh: 視平線就是眼睛的高度
tricks.body_en: Crouch and it drops. Climb and it rises.
tricks.body_zh: 蹲下它就降低，爬高它就升高。

tricks.title_en: Twice as far, half as tall
tricks.body_en: Three times as far, one third as tall.
tricks.body_zh: 三倍遠，就是三分之一高。

tricks.title_en: Below slopes up, above slopes down
tricks.title_zh: 低的往上斜，高的往下斜
tricks.body_en: Floor lines climb to the eye level. Ceiling lines come down to it.
tricks.body_zh: 地板的線往上斜向視平線；天花板的線往下斜向它。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: Never stand on or near a real railway track or in a road to look at perspective. Use a hallway, a sidewalk, or a photograph.
safety.zh: 絕對不要為了看透視而站到真的鐵軌上、鐵軌旁或馬路中間。請用走廊、人行道或照片。

safety.en: Ask an adult before you stand on a chair, and have someone hold it steady. Crouching is always safe.
safety.zh: 要站到椅子上之前先問大人，並請人扶穩。蹲下來看永遠是安全的。

safety.en: If you trace on a window, use a marker that wipes off, ask first, and do not lean on the glass.
safety.zh: 要在窗戶上描的話，用擦得掉的筆，先問過大人，而且不要靠在玻璃上。

safety.en: Rest your eyes: ten minutes after every thirty minutes of close work.
safety.zh: 讓眼睛休息：用眼每 30 分鐘休息 10 分鐘。

activities.title_en: Trace a Hallway on a Window
activities.title_zh: 把走廊描在一扇「窗戶」上

materials.en: A clear plastic sheet or folder, about the size of a notebook
materials.zh: 一片透明的塑膠片或資料夾，大約筆記本大小

materials.en: A marker that wipes off, and a ruler
materials.zh: 一支擦得掉的筆，和一把尺

materials.en: A long hallway, or a room with a tiled floor
materials.zh: 一條長走廊，或一間鋪了地磚的教室

materials.en: A partner
materials.zh: 一位同伴

steps.en: Stand at one end of the hallway. Your partner holds the clear sheet upright at arm's length in front of your face.
steps.zh: 站在走廊的一頭。請同伴把透明片立起來，舉在你面前一隻手臂遠的地方。

steps.en: Close one eye and keep your head still. Trace the edges of the floor and the ceiling as you see them through the sheet.
steps.zh: 閉上一隻眼睛，頭不要動。把透過透明片看到的地板邊線和天花板邊線描下來。

steps.en: Lay the sheet on a desk. Use the ruler to continue your lines until they cross. Mark the crossing.
steps.zh: 把透明片放到桌上，用尺把這些線延長到交叉為止，標出交點。

steps.en: Hold the sheet up again in the same place. What part of the hallway is behind your mark? How high is it compared with your eye?
steps.zh: 把透明片舉回原來的位置。交點後面是走廊的哪裡？和你的眼睛比起來，它有多高？

steps.en: Crouch and trace again in another color. Compare the two crossings, and then compare them with the model on this page.
steps.zh: 蹲下來，換一種顏色再描一次。比較兩個交點，再和這一頁的模型比一比。

activities.tip_en: Your lines may not cross at one neat point. A head that moves a little, or a second eye that opens, is enough to spoil it. That is what the model means by one eye that stays still.

activities.title_en: Draw a Hallway in One-Point Perspective
activities.title_zh: 用一點透視畫一條走廊

materials.en: White paper, a sharp pencil, an eraser, and a ruler
materials.zh: 白紙、削尖的鉛筆、橡皮擦和尺

materials.en: This page, with the model set to Line drawing

steps.en: Draw a light level line across the paper. This is your eye level. Put a dot on it for the vanishing point.
steps.zh: 在紙上輕輕畫一條水平線，這是你的視平線。在線上點一個點，當作消失點。

steps.en: Draw a small rectangle around the dot. This is the wall at the far end of the hallway.
steps.zh: 繞著那個點畫一個小長方形。這是走廊盡頭的牆。

steps.en: Lay the ruler from the vanishing point through each corner of the rectangle and draw outward to the edge of the paper. These four lines are the edges of the floor and the ceiling.
steps.zh: 把尺從消失點貼著長方形的每一個角，往外畫到紙的邊緣。這四條線就是地板和天花板的邊線。

steps.en: Add two doors on the side walls. Their tops and bottoms aim at the vanishing point, and their sides stand straight up.
steps.zh: 在兩邊的牆上各加一扇門。門的上緣和下緣對準消失點，門的兩側是垂直的。

steps.en: Set the model's eye to match your drawing and compare. Then draw the hallway again with the eye level much lower.
steps.zh: 把模型裡的眼睛調到和你的圖一樣的位置，比較一下。然後把視平線畫低很多，再畫一次。

activities.tip_en: Keep the first lines light so you can erase them. In one-point perspective only the lines that go into the distance are slanted. Lines that run across the picture stay level, and lines that stand up stay upright.
activities.tip_zh: 一開始的線畫輕一點，才擦得掉。在一點透視裡，只有往遠處去的線是斜的；橫過畫面的線保持水平，直立的線保持垂直。

lessons.title: How Do Painters Show Near and Far?
lessons.blurb_en: Five identical trees stand at five distances. Switch four cues on and off, overlap, size, position, and air, and watch a flat row of trees turn into a deep landscape.
lessons.blurb_zh: 五棵一模一樣的樹，立在五個不同的距離。把四種線索開開關關：重疊、大小、位置、空氣，看一排平平的樹怎麼變成有深度的風景。
lessons.big_idea_en: A painter has four simple cues for distance besides perspective lines. Near things cover far things. Far things are drawn smaller. On the ground, far things sit higher up the picture, toward the horizon. And far things look paler and bluer, because of the air between. Use none of them and the picture is flat. Use all four and it looks deep.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 除了透視線，畫家還有四種簡單的線索可以表現遠近：近的東西蓋住遠的；遠的東西畫得小；在地面上，遠的東西畫得比較高、靠近地平線；遠的東西看起來比較淡、比較藍，因為中間隔著空氣。一種都不用，畫面是平的；四種都用，畫面就有了深度。

lab.how_en: On the right is the world: five trees of the same size and color, standing 5, 8, 12, 18, and 27 meters from an eye. On the left is a picture of them. The four switches are the painter's choices. Turn a cue off and the picture stops using it, though the world stays the same. Every tree carries a number, 1 for the nearest, and the table gives the distance, drawn size, and lightness of each one.
lab.how_zh: 右邊是「世界」：五棵一樣大、一樣顏色的樹，離眼睛 5、8、12、18、27 公尺。左邊是把它們畫下來的一張「畫」。四個開關是畫家的選擇：關掉一種線索，畫面就不再用它，但世界並沒有改變。每棵樹都有編號（1 最近），表格寫出每一棵的距離、畫出來的大小和明度。

notes.en: The way the trees fade with distance follows a curve we chose. Real air depends on the weather, the moisture and dust in it, and the light. Distant things are usually bluish, and at sunrise or sunset they can turn reddish.
notes.zh: 樹隨著距離變淡的方式，照的是我們自己選的一條曲線。真實的空氣要看天氣、空氣裡的水氣和灰塵，還有光線。遠處的東西通常偏藍；日出或日落的時候，也可能偏紅。

notes.en: Twenty-seven meters of clear air would hardly change a tree's color. The model squeezes the effect of several kilometers into a short distance so that you can see it.
notes.zh: 27 公尺的乾淨空氣，幾乎不會改變一棵樹的顏色。模型把好幾公里才有的效果，壓縮到很短的距離裡，你才看得出來。

notes.en: The trees are flat cut-outs of one color, with no light and shade and no small details. Far things also lose detail, and the model does not show that.
notes.zh: 這些樹是單一顏色的平面剪影，沒有明暗，也沒有細節。遠處的東西還會失去細節，這一點模型沒有表現出來。

notes.en: The position cue here works for things standing on flat ground below your eye level. Clouds and birds above your eye level do the opposite: the far ones sit lower, toward the horizon.
notes.zh: 這裡的「位置」線索，適用於站在平地上、比眼睛低的東西。比眼睛高的雲和鳥正好相反：遠的畫得比較低，同樣是靠近地平線。

lab.note_end_en: So look out of a real window at real hills or buildings. Classroom Activity 1 shows what to look for.
lab.note_end_zh: 所以請從真的窗戶往外看，看真的山或房子；要看什麼，寫在課堂活動一。
lab.credit_html: Trees and landscape made for this lesson. The colors and positions are computed by shared code and covered by automatic tests. · 樹與風景為本課自行繪製；顏色與位置由共用的程式計算，並有自動測試。

paras: Draw five trees in a row, all the same size, all the same green, all standing on one line. Your picture is flat. Nothing in it says which tree is close and which is far. Yet a landscape painter can make you feel that one hill is a short walk away and another is a day's journey. Painters do it with a small set of cues, and you already read every one of them without thinking.

The first cue is overlap. If one tree hides part of another, the hidden one must be behind. Overlap tells you the order of things, though it cannot tell you how far apart they are. The second cue is size. When you know two trees are about the same size, the one that looks smaller seems farther away. This is the rule you met in Lesson 5: twice as far, half as tall.

The third cue is position on the picture. Look at a field or a floor. The ground near your feet is at the bottom of your view, and the ground far away is higher up, close to the horizon. So a tree whose foot is drawn higher on the picture looks farther off. This works for things on the ground, below your eye level. Clouds above you do the opposite.

The fourth cue is the air itself. Air scatters sunlight, and that scattered light is added to everything you see through it. The more air lies between you and a hill, the paler the hill looks, and the less contrast it has. Scattered sky light usually has more blue in it, so far hills usually look bluish. Artists call this aerial perspective, or atmospheric perspective.

Leonardo da Vinci wrote about it in his notebooks about five hundred years ago. He called it aerial perspective, because, he said, the atmosphere lets us tell how far away different buildings are. His advice to painters was plain. Paint the nearest building in its real color, and make the more distant ones less defined and bluer.

Chinese landscape painters thought about distance too. In the eleventh century the painter Guo Xi described three kinds of distance in a mountain scene: looking up from the foot of a mountain to its peak, looking from the front of a mountain to what lies behind, and looking from a near mountain across to far ones. All these painters, east and west, were solving the same puzzle. The paper is flat, and the world is not.
paras_zh: 畫五棵樹排成一排，一樣大、一樣綠，站在同一條線上。你的畫是平的，畫面上沒有任何東西說明哪一棵近、哪一棵遠。可是風景畫家卻能讓你覺得，這座山走幾步就到，那座山要走上一整天。畫家靠的是少少幾種線索，而每一種你其實早就會讀了，連想都不用想。
第一種線索是重疊。如果一棵樹擋住另一棵的一部分，被擋住的那一棵一定在後面。重疊告訴你東西的前後順序，但說不出它們相隔多遠。第二種線索是大小。當你知道兩棵樹差不多一樣大的時候，看起來比較小的那一棵，就顯得比較遠。這是第五課遇過的規則：兩倍遠，一半高。
第三種線索是在畫面上的位置。看看一片田野或地板：腳邊的地面在視野的最下面，遠處的地面比較高，靠近地平線。所以一棵樹的底部畫得越高，看起來就越遠。這只適用於地面上、比眼睛低的東西；頭頂上的雲正好相反。
第四種線索是空氣本身。空氣會散射陽光，而這些被散射的光，會疊加在你透過空氣看到的每一樣東西上。你和一座山之間的空氣越多，山看起來就越淡，對比也越低。被散射的天空光通常藍色的成分比較多，所以遠山通常看起來偏藍。藝術家把這叫做空氣透視，也叫大氣透視。
大約五百年前，達文西在筆記裡寫過這件事。他把它叫做空氣透視，因為他說，靠著大氣，我們才分得出不同的建築各有多遠。他給畫家的建議很直接：最近的建築畫它本來的顏色，比較遠的就畫得模糊一點、藍一點。
中國的山水畫家也思考過遠近。十一世紀的畫家郭熙說，山有三種「遠」：從山下仰望山頂，從山前看到山後，從近山望向遠山。東方和西方的這些畫家，解的是同一道難題：紙是平的，世界卻不是。
questions: Overlap shows that one tree is behind another. What can it not tell you?
Two trees are the same real size, but one is drawn half as tall as the other. What does that tell you?
Why do far hills usually look paler and bluer than near ones?
answers: It cannot tell you how far apart the two trees are. Overlap gives only the order, which one is in front.
The smaller one is farther away. If they really are the same size, it is about twice as far from your eye.

Air scatters sunlight, and that scattered light is added between you and the hills. More air means more added light, so the hills look paler. The scattered light usually has more blue in it, so they look bluish.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.meta_en: Add the cues one at a time
parts.text_en: All four cues start switched off: five trees in a flat row. Then overlap, size, position, and air come on one after another.
parts.text_zh: 四種線索一開始全部關掉：五棵樹排成平平的一排。接著重疊、大小、位置、空氣一種一種打開。

parts.text_en: Only the air cue is on. The trees are the same size and stand on one line, yet the pale ones already look farther away.
parts.text_zh: 只打開「空氣」這一種。五棵樹一樣大、站在同一條線上，可是淡的那幾棵已經顯得比較遠了。

parts.meta_en: From the side, then from above
parts.text_en: Seen from the side, the five trees are thin slices set one behind another, like a paper theater. From above you can read their real distances.
parts.text_zh: 從側面看，五棵樹是一片一片前後排開的薄片，像紙劇場。從上面看，可以讀出它們真正的距離。

parts.text_en: Look at the world from the eye, through the picture frame. Overlap, size, and position are already there before the painter does anything.
parts.text_zh: 從眼睛的位置、透過畫框去看世界。畫家什麼都還沒做，重疊、大小和位置就已經在裡面了。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Which single cue gives the strongest feeling of depth for you? Which two cues work best together? Compare your answer with a classmate's.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。對你來說，哪一種線索單獨使用時，深度的感覺最強？哪兩種搭配起來效果最好？和同學比較一下答案。

far.lead_en: Eight pictures of two trees, A and B. They are really the same size and the same color. Each picture uses just one cue. Choose the tree that looks farther away, and the page will tell you which cue you were reading.
far.lead_zh: 八張圖，每張有 A、B 兩棵樹。它們實際上一樣大、一樣顏色；每張圖只用一種線索。選出看起來比較遠的那一棵，頁面會告訴你剛才讀的是哪一種線索。
far.note_en: Psychologists call these monocular cues, because they work with one eye and in flat pictures.
far.note_zh: 心理學家把這些叫做單眼線索，因為只用一隻眼睛、看的是平面的圖，它們也有效。

arrange.lead_en: Three trees, A, B, and C, each with a slider. Place 1 is the nearest and place 5 is the farthest. Move the trees to finish three small tasks. As a tree goes back, watch all four cues change together: it shrinks, rises, fades, and slips behind the others.
arrange.lead_zh: A、B、C 三棵樹，各有一根滑桿。位置 1 最近，位置 5 最遠。移動它們，完成三個小任務。一棵樹往後退的時候，注意四種線索一起變：它變小、升高、變淡，而且躲到別棵的後面。
arrange.note_en: When two trees are at the same distance, they are drawn the same size and the same color, and the picture cannot tell you which is in front.
arrange.note_zh: 兩棵樹在同樣的距離時，畫出來一樣大、一樣顏色，畫面就說不出哪一棵在前面。

culture_cards.title_en: Leonardo's blue mountains, Guo Xi's three distances, size that means importance, and the air above your town
culture_cards.title_zh: 達文西的藍色遠山、郭熙的三遠、代表地位的大小，和你頭頂的空氣
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people have noticed distance and put it into pictures.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人怎麼注意到遠近、又怎麼把它放進畫裡的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: In his notebooks Leonardo da Vinci wrote: “There is another kind of perspective which I call Aerial Perspective, because by the atmosphere we are able to distinguish the variations in distance of different buildings.” He also asked why far mountains look blue. He argued that the air itself is not blue: it takes on that color, he wrote, from particles of moisture that catch the rays of the sun.
cards.body_zh: 達文西在筆記裡寫道：「還有另一種透視，我稱它為空氣透視，因為靠著大氣，我們才分得出不同建築遠近的差別。」他也問過遠山為什麼是藍的。他認為空氣本身並不是藍色的；他寫道，空氣是因為其中的水氣微粒截住了陽光，才帶上那種顏色。

cards.body_en: The painter Guo Xi wrote that a mountain has three distances. Looking up from the foot to the peak is high distance. Looking from the front of the mountain to what lies behind is deep distance. Looking from a near mountain to far ones is level distance. A Taiwanese education encyclopedia notes that one Chinese landscape often holds all three at once, because it does not keep to a single viewpoint.
cards.body_zh: 郭熙在《林泉高致》裡說：「山有三遠：自山下而仰山顛，謂之『高遠』；自山前而窺山後，謂之『深遠』；自近山而望遠山，謂之『平遠』。」《教育大辭書》指出，中國山水畫不採單點透視，所以一個畫面裡往往同時具備三遠的空間表現。

cards.body_en: Size has not always stood for distance. In the art of ancient Egypt, people of higher status were sometimes drawn larger than those of lower status. This is called hierarchical proportion. Egyptian artists did use simple overlapping to show which figure was nearer. A cue is a habit shared by the artist and the viewer, and different times have used the same cue for different jobs.
cards.body_zh: 大小並不是一直都代表遠近。在古埃及的藝術裡，地位高的人有時畫得比地位低的人大，這叫做階級比例。不過埃及的畫師確實用簡單的重疊，來表示哪一個人物比較近。線索是畫的人和看的人共有的習慣；不同的時代，會拿同一種線索做不同的事。

cards.body_en: Molecules of air, and larger particles such as water vapor and smoke, scatter light. This scattered sky light is laid like a thin veil over the light coming from a distant hill, and it lowers the hill's contrast. Sky light usually has more short-wavelength light in it, which is also why the sky looks blue, so distant things usually look bluish. On a hazy day the veil is thicker, and the hills fade sooner.
cards.body_zh: 空氣的分子，還有水氣、煙塵這些比較大的微粒，都會散射光。這些被散射的天空光，像一層薄紗蓋在遠山傳來的光上面，讓遠山的對比降低。天空光裡短波長的光通常比較多（這也是天空看起來是藍色的原因），所以遠處的東西通常偏藍。霧霾重的日子，這層薄紗比較厚，山也就更快淡掉。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The visual arts curriculum does not name these cues. These are the closest entries, with one from science, and their links to this lesson are our reading of them.
curric.lead_zh: 視覺藝術課綱的條文沒有點名這些線索。下面是最接近的條目，另外加上自然科學的一條；它們和這一課的連結，是本教材的解讀。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小三、四年級）
items.text: 色彩感知、造形與空間的探索。
items.note_en: Overlap, size, and position are ways to explore space, and aerial perspective links space to color.
items.note_zh: 重疊、大小和位置是探索空間的方法；空氣透視則把空間和色彩連在一起。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 視覺元素、色彩與構成要素的辨識與溝通。
items.note_en: Words such as foreground, background, and overlap let students say how a picture is built.
items.note_zh: 前景、背景、重疊這些詞，讓學生能說出一張圖是怎麼組成的。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 藝術語彙、形式原理與視覺美感。
items.note_en: Reading the cues for distance is part of looking closely at a landscape painting.
items.note_zh: 讀出表現遠近的線索，是仔細看一幅風景畫的一部分。

items.area: 自然科學領域（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 陽光是由不同色光組成。
items.note_en: Air scatters the blue part of sunlight more than the rest, which is where aerial perspective begins.
items.note_zh: 空氣把陽光裡藍色的部分散射得比其他顏色多；空氣透視就是從這裡開始的。

myths.myth_en: Far hills look blue because air is blue.
myths.myth_zh: 遠山是藍的，因為空氣是藍色的。
myths.fact_en: Air scatters sunlight, and the scattered light, which usually has more blue in it, is added between you and the hills. At sunrise or sunset the added light can be reddish. Leonardo already argued that the air itself is not blue.
myths.fact_zh: 空氣會散射陽光，被散射的光通常藍色成分比較多，疊加在你和遠山之間。日出或日落時，疊加的光也可能偏紅。達文西當年就主張，空氣本身並不是藍色的。

myths.myth_en: Anything drawn higher on the picture is farther away.
myths.myth_zh: 畫在畫面上越高的東西，就越遠。
myths.fact_en: That holds for things on the ground, below your eye level: far ground is nearer the horizon. Above your eye level it is reversed. A far cloud sits lower than a near one, and it too is nearer the horizon.
myths.fact_zh: 這只適用於地面上、比眼睛低的東西：遠處的地面比較靠近地平線。比眼睛高的東西正好相反：遠的雲比近的雲低，同樣是比較靠近地平線。

myths.myth_en: A bigger figure in a picture is always a nearer one.
myths.myth_zh: 畫裡比較大的人物，一定比較近。
myths.fact_en: Only when the artist is using size for distance. In ancient Egyptian art, a larger figure was often a more important person. You have to know which habit the picture follows.
myths.fact_zh: 只有在畫的人用大小來表現遠近的時候才是這樣。在古埃及的藝術裡，畫得比較大的往往是地位比較高的人。要先知道這張圖用的是哪一種習慣。

myths.myth_en: Without perspective lines, a picture cannot look deep.
myths.myth_zh: 沒有透視線，畫面就不可能有深度。
myths.fact_en: Overlap, size, position, and air need no ruler and no vanishing point. Landscapes with no straight lines at all can look very deep. The model on this page has no perspective lines in it.
myths.fact_zh: 重疊、大小、位置和空氣，都不需要尺，也不需要消失點。完全沒有直線的風景，也可以看起來很深。這一頁的模型裡就沒有任何透視線。

tricks_head.en: Near and far in a sentence

tricks.body_en: If part of a thing is hidden, something nearer is hiding it.
tricks.body_zh: 一樣東西有一部分被擋住，擋住它的那個就比較近。

tricks.body_en: Twice as far, half as tall.
tricks.body_zh: 兩倍遠，一半高。

tricks.title_en: Far ground climbs to the horizon
tricks.title_zh: 遠處的地面往地平線爬
tricks.body_en: On the ground, a higher foot is a farther foot.
tricks.body_zh: 在地面上，底部畫得越高，就越遠。

tricks.body_en: More air between, less contrast and more sky color.
tricks.body_zh: 中間的空氣越多，對比越低，越帶著天空的顏色。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: Never look at the Sun, not even through a window or through haze. Look at hills and buildings away from it.
safety.zh: 絕對不要看太陽，隔著窗戶或隔著霧霾也不行。請看離太陽遠一點的山和房子。

safety.en: Look from a safe place: a classroom window, a balcony with a railing, or the playground. Do not lean out or climb on anything to see farther.
safety.zh: 在安全的地方看：教室的窗邊、有欄杆的陽台，或操場。不要為了看得更遠而探出身體或爬到東西上面。

safety.en: Carry scissors closed, with the points down, and hand them to someone handle first.
safety.zh: 拿剪刀走動時要合起來、尖端朝下；遞給別人時握柄朝向對方。

safety.en: Looking far is good for your eyes. Rest them for ten minutes after every thirty minutes of close work.
safety.zh: 看遠方對眼睛有好處。用眼每 30 分鐘，就休息 10 分鐘。

activities.title_en: Count the Layers Out of a Window

materials.en: A window or a high place with a long view of hills, buildings, or rows of trees
materials.zh: 一扇窗戶或一個高處，看得到一層一層的山、房子或成排的樹

materials.en: Paper and a pencil
materials.zh: 紙和鉛筆

materials.en: This page, with the model's table showing
materials.zh: 這一頁，模型的表格開著

steps.en: Find a view with at least three layers, such as trees close by, buildings farther off, and hills behind them.
steps.zh: 找一個至少有三層的景：例如近處的樹、遠一點的房子、更後面的山。

steps.en: Draw one box for each layer, nearest at the bottom. In each box write what the layer is.
steps.zh: 每一層畫一個格子，最近的放在最下面。在格子裡寫下那一層是什麼。

steps.en: For each layer, write one word for its color and one word for how sharp its edges are.
steps.zh: 替每一層寫下一個形容顏色的詞，和一個形容邊緣清不清楚的詞。

steps.en: Mark every place where one layer covers part of another.
steps.zh: 標出每一個「這一層蓋住另一層」的地方。

steps.en: Compare your notes with the model. Do your far layers get paler? Bluer? Look again on a hazy day and on a clear day.
steps.zh: 把你的紀錄和模型比一比。你看到的遠處，有沒有變淡？有沒有變藍？霧濛濛的日子和晴朗的日子各看一次。

activities.tip_en: You may find that your far layers are gray or brownish and hardly blue at all. That is a real result. The color of the haze depends on the weather, on what is in the air, and on where the Sun is. Write down what you see, and do not write what the model says you should see.
activities.tip_zh: 你可能會發現，遠處那幾層是灰的或偏褐色，幾乎不藍。這是真實的結果：霧霾的顏色要看天氣、空氣裡有什麼，還有太陽在哪裡。請寫下你看到的，不要寫模型說你「應該」看到的。

activities.title_en: A Landscape in Four Layers of Paper

materials.en: Four sheets of paper in one color family, from dark to very pale, or white paper and one watercolor
materials.zh: 同一個色系、由深到很淺的四張紙；或白紙加一種水彩

materials.en: A sheet of pale blue or white paper for the sky
materials.zh: 一張淡藍或白色的紙，當作天空

materials.en: Scissors and glue
materials.zh: 剪刀和膠水

steps.en: If you are using watercolor, paint four strips with more and more water, so that they go from dark to very pale. Let them dry.
steps.zh: 如果用水彩，就畫四條紙帶，水越加越多，讓顏色由深到很淡。等它們乾。

steps.en: Cut a row of hills from each sheet. Make the palest hills the smallest and the darkest hills the largest.
steps.zh: 從每一張紙上剪出一排山。最淡的剪得最小，最深的剪得最大。

steps.en: Glue the palest row highest on the sky paper. Glue each darker row a little lower, so that it covers the foot of the row behind.
steps.zh: 把最淡的那一排貼在天空紙上最高的地方。越深的貼得越低，並蓋住後面那一排的底部。

steps.en: Stand back. Which of the four cues did you use? Write them on the back.
steps.zh: 退後幾步看。四種線索你用了哪幾種？寫在背面。

steps.en: Now make a second picture that breaks one cue, for example with the palest hills in front. Show both to a classmate and ask which looks deeper.
steps.zh: 再做第二張，故意破壞其中一種線索，例如把最淡的山貼在最前面。把兩張都拿給同學看，問哪一張看起來比較深。

activities.tip_en: Compare your paper landscape with the picture on this page. The screen makes its pale colors with light, and your paper makes them with pigment or with more water, so the two will not match exactly. What matters is the order from dark to pale.
activities.tip_zh: 把你的紙風景和這一頁的畫比一比。螢幕的淡色是用光做出來的，你的紙是用色料或加水做出來的，兩者不會完全一樣。重要的是由深到淡的順序。

links.zh: 怎麼在平面上畫出一個房間？

lessons.title: Where Should the Main Thing Go?
lessons.blurb_en: A picture has edges, and where you put things inside them changes how the picture feels. Drag shapes around a frame, watch the balance point move, and crop a wide scene in three different ways.
lessons.blurb_zh: 畫面有邊，東西放在邊框裡的哪裡，會改變整張畫給人的感覺。在畫框裡拖動形狀，看重心怎麼移動；再把一片寬寬的風景，用三種方式裁切。
lessons.big_idea_en: A picture is a rectangle with edges. Where you place things inside it changes its balance and decides what the viewer looks at first. A big pale shape near the middle can balance a small dark shape far out, like a seesaw. The main thing does not have to be in the center, and it does not have to be on a thirds line either. The empty space around it is part of the picture too.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 畫面是一個有邊的長方形。東西放在裡面的哪裡，會改變畫面的平衡，也決定看的人先看哪裡。靠近中間的大而淡的形狀，可以和放得遠遠的小而深的形狀互相平衡，就像蹺蹺板。主角不一定要放在正中央，也不一定要放在三分線上。它四周空著的地方，也是畫面的一部分。

lab.title_en: A Frame and a Balance Point
lab.how_en: Drag the gray shapes around the frame, or select one and move it with the arrow keys. The yellow diamond ◆ marks the picture's balance point, and the seesaw below it tips toward the heavier side. Try the five ways to arrange, then switch on the thirds lines. There is no 3D in this lesson, on purpose. A picture is flat, and this lesson is about the flat rectangle itself.
lab.how_zh: 在畫框裡拖動灰色的形狀，或選取一個、用方向鍵移動。黃色的菱形 ◆ 標出畫面的重心，下面的蹺蹺板會往比較重的那一邊傾斜。試試五種擺法，再打開三分線。這一課刻意不用 3D：畫是平的，這一課講的就是這個平平的長方形。

notes.en: The weight of each shape is a formula we chose: its area in the frame times how much darker it is than the paper. There is no agreed formula for visual weight.
notes.zh: 每個形狀的重量，是我們自己選的公式：它在畫框裡的面積，乘上它比紙深多少。視覺重量並沒有公認的公式。

notes.en: In real pictures, color, direction, and meaning add weight too. People tend to look at faces and words. The model has none of these.
notes.zh: 在真的畫裡，顏色、方向和意義也會增加重量。人特別容易去看臉和文字。模型裡這些都沒有。

notes.en: The page calls a picture balanced when its balance point is within 6% of the middle. That line is our choice, and your eye may disagree.
notes.zh: 頁面把重心離中央 6% 以內的畫面叫做「平衡」。這條線是我們自己畫的，你的眼睛可能有不同的看法。

notes.en: The model only looks at left and right. Top and bottom balance matter too, and so does the empty space between the shapes.
notes.zh: 模型只看左右。上下的平衡也很重要，形狀之間空著的地方也是。

lab.note_end_en: So test it with real paper and real eyes. Classroom Activity 2 asks your classmates which arrangement looks balanced, and then compares their answers with the model.
lab.note_end_zh: 所以請用真的紙和真的眼睛來檢驗。課堂活動二請同學判斷哪一種擺法看起來平衡，再和模型的答案比一比。
lab.credit_html: Shapes and scene made for this lesson. The balance point is computed by shared code and covered by automatic tests. · 形狀與風景為本課自行繪製；重心由共用的程式計算，並有自動測試。

paras: Every picture has edges. A painting has a frame, a photo has borders, and a page in your sketchbook stops where the paper stops. Inside those edges, the artist decides where everything goes. This is called composition. Move the main thing a little to the left, or make the empty space a little larger, and the whole picture feels different.

One thing artists think about is balance. Some shapes look heavier than others. A big shape looks heavier than a small one, and on light paper a dark shape looks heavier than a pale one. When the heavy parts are all on one side, the picture seems to tip over. When they are spread out well, it feels steady.

There are three main kinds of balance. In symmetrical balance, the two sides are like mirror images. In asymmetrical balance, the two sides are different but still look balanced. A big pale shape near the middle can balance a small dark shape far out, just as a light child at the far end of a seesaw can balance a heavier child sitting near the middle. In radial balance, things spread out from a center, like the petals of a flower.

Artists also decide what should catch your eye first. This is called emphasis, and the place you look at first is the focal point. An artist can make one area stand out by making it different from everything around it. Scientists who track people's eyes have found that faces and words pull our eyes strongly, even when we are asked to look for something else.

You may have heard of the rule of thirds. Draw two lines across the picture and two lines down it, so that it is cut into nine equal parts, and put the main thing on one of the lines or where two of them cross. The name was first written down in 1797. It is a rule of thumb, not a law. Many fine pictures put the main thing right in the middle.

Finally, look at what is not there. The empty space around and between things is called negative space, and it has a shape of its own. Chinese calligraphers say that the blank parts of a character should be planned as carefully as the brush strokes. A picture with lots of empty space can feel calm, and a crowded one can feel busy. Neither is wrong. It depends on what the artist wants you to feel.
paras_zh: 每一張畫都有邊。油畫有畫框，照片有邊緣，素描本的一頁到紙的邊就停了。在這些邊的裡面，東西要放在哪裡，由畫的人決定。這叫做構圖。把主角往左移一點，或把空白留大一點，整張畫的感覺就不一樣了。
畫家會考慮的一件事是平衡。有些形狀看起來比別的重：大的看起來比小的重；在淺色的紙上，深的看起來也比淡的重。重的部分全擠在同一邊，畫面就好像要倒了；分配得好，畫面就感覺很穩。
平衡主要有三種。對稱的平衡，兩邊就像鏡子裡的影像。不對稱的平衡，兩邊不一樣，看起來卻還是平衡的：靠近中間的大而淡的形狀，可以和放得遠遠的小而深的形狀互相平衡，就像蹺蹺板上，坐在最尾端的輕的小孩，可以和坐在靠近中間的重的小孩平衡一樣。放射狀的平衡，東西從一個中心往外排開，像花的花瓣。
畫家也會決定什麼東西要先抓住你的目光。這叫做強調，你最先看的地方叫做焦點。畫家可以讓某一塊和周圍都不一樣，讓它跳出來。追蹤眼睛的科學家發現，臉和文字特別會吸引我們的目光，就算我們被要求去找別的東西也一樣。
你可能聽過三分法：在畫面上畫兩條橫線、兩條直線，把它分成一樣大的九格，再把主角放在其中一條線上，或兩條線的交點上。這個名稱最早在 1797 年被寫下來。它是經驗法則，不是定律；很多很好的畫，主角就放在正中央。
最後，看看沒有東西的地方。東西四周和中間空著的地方叫做負空間，它也有自己的形狀。中國的書法講「計白當黑」：字裡空白的地方，要像筆畫一樣用心安排。空白多的畫面可以感覺很安靜，擠滿東西的畫面可以感覺很熱鬧。兩種都沒有錯，要看畫的人想讓你感受到什麼。
questions: What is the difference between symmetrical and asymmetrical balance?
How can a small shape balance a much bigger one?
Is the rule of thirds a law that every good picture follows?
answers: In symmetrical balance the two sides are like mirror images. In asymmetrical balance the two sides are different, but the picture still looks balanced.
Make the small shape darker, so it looks heavier, and put it farther from the middle, like a light child at the far end of a seesaw.
No. It is a rule of thumb that was first written down in 1797. Many fine pictures put the main thing in the middle, and studies have not found that the rule makes pictures better.

vocab.ex: The composition puts the boat on the right.
vocab.exzh: 這張畫的構圖把船放在右邊。

vocab.ex: The two trees give the picture balance.
vocab.exzh: 兩棵樹讓畫面平衡。

vocab.ex: A butterfly is symmetrical.
vocab.exzh: 蝴蝶是對稱的。

vocab.ex: The cat is at the edge of the frame.
vocab.exzh: 貓在畫面的邊上。

vocab.ex: The red door is the focal point of the painting.
vocab.exzh: 紅色的門是這幅畫的焦點。

vocab.ex: The bright light gives emphasis to her face.
vocab.exzh: 明亮的光強調了她的臉。

vocab.ex: The negative space around the bird makes it look alone.
vocab.exzh: 鳥四周的空白讓牠看起來很孤單。

vocab.ex: She cropped the photo to cut out the road.
vocab.exzh: 她把照片裁掉一部分，把馬路切掉了。

options: Right next to it, on the same side
Far out on the other side

quiz.q: What is the empty space around and between things called?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Everything starts crowded on the left. Then the big pale shape slides toward the middle and the small dark shape moves far out to the right, until the seesaw levels.
parts.text_zh: 一開始全部擠在左邊。接著大而淡的形狀往中間移，小而深的形狀移到右邊很遠的地方，直到蹺蹺板變平。

parts.text_en: The left half is a mirror image of the right half, so the balance point sits exactly on the center line.
parts.text_zh: 左半邊是右半邊的鏡像，所以重心剛好落在中線上。

parts.text_en: Seven circles spread out evenly from the middle, like petals. Drag one away and watch the balance tip.
parts.text_zh: 七個圓從中間均勻地往外排開，像花瓣。拖走其中一個，看重心怎麼偏。

parts.text_en: The thirds lines appear, and the small dark shape moves to the point where two lines cross.
parts.text_zh: 三分線出現了，小而深的形狀移到兩條線交叉的點上。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then make your own picture. Put the small dark shape right in the middle, then on a thirds point. Which do you like better? Ask a classmate too. You may not agree, and that is fine.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己排一張。把小而深的形狀放在正中央，再放到三分點上。你比較喜歡哪一張？也問問同學。你們可能意見不同，這沒有關係。

bal.lead_en: Six pairs of pictures. Decide which one of each pair looks more balanced. Then the page shows where each balance point ◆ is and explains why.
bal.lead_zh: 六組圖。每一組選出看起來比較平衡的那一張；接著頁面會標出兩張的重心 ◆ 在哪裡，並說明原因。
bal.note_en: The page checks your answer with the same model as above. If your eye disagrees with the model, your eye is not wrong. Write down why.
bal.note_zh: 頁面用的是上面那個模型來對答案。如果你的眼睛和模型意見不同，不代表你的眼睛錯了，把原因寫下來。

crop.lead_en: A wide scene with a boat, a tree, a house, and the sun. Move and resize the yellow frame to finish three tasks. The same scene can make very different pictures, depending on what you keep and what you cut.
crop.lead_zh: 一片寬寬的風景，有船、樹、房子和太陽。移動黃色的框、改變它的大小，完成三個任務。同一片風景，留下什麼、切掉什麼，就會變成很不一樣的畫面。
crop.note_en: The frame always keeps the shape of a 4:3 rectangle, like many photos and screens.
crop.note_zh: 裁切框的形狀固定是 4:3 的長方形，和很多照片、螢幕一樣。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Frame · 畫框背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A rule named in 1797, eyes that follow questions, blank space in calligraphy, and rules put to the test
culture_cards.title_zh: 1797 年取名的規則、跟著問題走的眼睛、書法裡的空白，以及接受檢驗的規則
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about where people put things in a picture, and how we know what works.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事：人怎麼決定東西放在畫面的哪裡，以及我們怎麼知道哪樣行得通。

cards.body_en: In 1797 the English artist John Thomas Smith wrote about a “Rule of thirds” in a book called Remarks on Rural Scenery. He meant it for landscapes: let the sky take up about two-thirds of the picture, or about one-third, instead of exactly half. Not everyone agreed. In 1845 another writer, George Field, called the rule “neither accurate nor universal.”
cards.body_zh: 1797 年，英國的畫家史密斯（John Thomas Smith）在《鄉村風景評述》這本書裡寫到「三分法」。他指的是風景畫：讓天空大約占畫面的三分之二，或大約三分之一，而不是剛好一半。並不是每個人都同意。1845 年，另一位作者菲爾德（George Field）說這條規則「既不精確，也不普遍」。

cards.body_en: The Russian scientist Alfred Yarbus recorded where people's eyes went as they looked at pictures. He found that the path of the eyes depended on what the viewer had been asked to do. When people looked at a face, their eyes kept going back to the eyes and the mouth. So there is no single path that every viewer's eyes follow through a picture.
cards.body_zh: 俄國科學家亞布斯（Alfred Yarbus）記錄人看圖時眼睛往哪裡看。他發現，眼睛走的路線要看看的人被要求做什麼。人看一張臉時，目光會一再回到眼睛和嘴巴。所以，並沒有一條每個人的眼睛都會照著走的路線。

cards.body_en: Chinese calligraphy has a saying, “count the white as black” (計白當黑). The Ministry of Education's dictionary explains that it means arranging the blank spaces within and between characters as carefully as if they were real brush strokes, so that the space is well balanced. The same idea works in a picture. The empty part is something you design.
cards.body_zh: 中國書法講「計白當黑」。《重編國語辭典修訂本》的解釋是：書法上指將字裡行間中的空白處，當做實體筆畫一般安排布置，務使空間調配得當。畫面也是一樣：空著的部分，也是要設計的。

cards.en: Putting the rules to the test
cards.body_en: Do the rules really work? In 2014 a team of scientists checked large sets of high-quality photographs and paintings. They found that the rule of thirds seems to play only a minor role, if any. In another study, when people framed a single object facing the viewer, they liked it best at or near the center. Rules can help you start, but your eyes have the last word.
cards.body_zh: 這些規則真的有用嗎？2014 年，一組科學家檢查了大量的優秀照片和畫作，發現三分法似乎只扮演很小的角色，甚至沒有角色。另一個研究發現，當人替一個正對著觀眾的東西取景時，最喜歡把它放在正中央或靠近中央。規則可以幫你起頭，但最後要由你的眼睛決定。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: The arts curriculum does not use the word composition (構圖). It speaks of the elements and principles of form (構成要素、形式原理). These are the closest entries, and their links to this lesson are our reading of them.
curric.lead_zh: 藝術領域課綱的條文沒有用「構圖」這個詞，用的是「構成要素」和「形式原理」。下面是最接近的條目；它們和這一課的連結，是本教材的解讀。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術 學習內容（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 視覺元素、色彩與構成要素的辨識與溝通。
items.note_en: Balance, focal point, and negative space are words for talking about how a picture is put together.
items.note_zh: 平衡、焦點、負空間，都是用來說明一張圖怎麼組成的詞。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術 學習內容（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 藝術語彙、形式原理與視覺美感。
items.note_en: Balance and emphasis are among the principles of form.
items.note_zh: 平衡和強調都屬於形式原理。

items.area: 藝術領域 學習表現（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 能發現藝術作品中的構成要素與形式原理，並表達自己的想法。
items.note_en: The balance game asks students to judge first and explain afterward.
items.note_zh: 「哪一張比較平衡」先請學生自己判斷，再說出理由。

items.area: 藝術領域・視覺藝術 學習表現（國中）
items.text: 能使用構成要素和形式原理，表達情感與想法。
items.note_en: Calm empty space and busy crowded space are choices that carry feeling.
items.note_zh: 安靜的空白和熱鬧的擁擠，都是帶著情感的選擇。

myths.myth_en: Never put the main thing in the middle.
myths.myth_zh: 主角絕對不能放在正中間。
myths.fact_en: Many fine pictures do. In one study, when people framed a single object facing the viewer, they liked it best at or near the center. The middle feels steady and still, which is sometimes exactly what the artist wants.
myths.fact_zh: 很多很好的畫就是這樣放的。有一個研究發現，人替一個正對著觀眾的東西取景時，最喜歡放在正中央或靠近中央。中間給人穩定、安靜的感覺，有時正是畫的人想要的。

myths.myth_en: The rule of thirds is a law of good pictures.
myths.myth_zh: 三分法是好畫面的定律。
myths.fact_en: It is a rule of thumb from 1797. A 2014 study of large sets of photographs and paintings found that it seems to play only a minor role, if any.
myths.fact_zh: 它是 1797 年留下來的經驗法則。2014 年一個檢查大量照片和畫作的研究發現，它似乎只扮演很小的角色，甚至沒有角色。

myths.myth_en: Famous paintings, like the Mona Lisa, were built on the golden ratio.
myths.myth_zh: 名畫（例如〈蒙娜麗莎〉）都是照黃金比例畫的。
myths.fact_en: The claim about the Mona Lisa is not supported by Leonardo's own writings, and careful tests of whether people prefer the golden ratio have been inconclusive at best.
myths.fact_zh: 〈蒙娜麗莎〉用了黃金比例的說法，在達文西自己的文字裡找不到根據；仔細檢驗人是否偏好黃金比例的研究，結果最多只能說沒有定論。

myths.myth_en: Empty space is wasted space.
myths.myth_zh: 空白就是浪費掉的地方。
myths.fact_en: Negative space has a shape of its own, and it decides how calm or crowded a picture feels. Chinese calligraphers plan the blank parts as carefully as the strokes.
myths.fact_zh: 負空間有自己的形狀，也決定畫面感覺安靜還是擁擠。中國的書法家安排空白，就像安排筆畫一樣用心。

tricks.title_en: Big and pale near, small and dark far
tricks.title_zh: 大淡靠中間，小深放遠邊
tricks.body_en: That is how a seesaw balances.
tricks.body_zh: 蹺蹺板就是這樣平衡的。

tricks.body_en: The focal point is the part that is unlike the rest.
tricks.body_zh: 焦點就是和其他部分不一樣的那一塊。

tricks.title_en: Thirds are a start, not a law
tricks.title_zh: 三分法是起點，不是定律
tricks.body_en: Try it, then try the middle, and trust your eyes.
tricks.body_zh: 試試看，也試試正中央，最後相信你的眼睛。

tricks.body_en: Count the white as black.
tricks.body_zh: 計白當黑。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: Use scissors to cut the viewfinder. If a craft knife is needed for the window, an adult should do that part.
safety.zh: 用剪刀剪取景框。如果挖窗口需要美工刀，那一部分請大人來做。

safety.en: Carry scissors closed, with the points down, and hand them to someone handle first.
safety.zh: 拿剪刀走動時要合起來、尖端朝下；遞給別人時握柄朝向對方。

safety.en: When you walk around looking through a viewfinder, stop before you look. Do not walk while your eye is at the window.
safety.zh: 拿著取景框到處看的時候，先停下來再看。眼睛貼在窗口上時不要走路。

safety.en: Never look at the Sun through the viewfinder or in any other way.
safety.zh: 不要透過取景框看太陽，用任何方式都不行。

materials.en: A piece of card about the size of a postcard
materials.zh: 一張大約明信片大小的卡紙

materials.en: Scissors and a ruler
materials.zh: 剪刀和尺

materials.en: Paper and a pencil
materials.zh: 紙和鉛筆

steps.en: Cut a window 8 cm wide and 6 cm high in the middle of the card. That is the same 4:3 shape as the frame on this page.
steps.zh: 在卡紙中間挖一個寬 8 公分、高 6 公分的窗口。這和本頁畫框一樣是 4:3 的形狀。

steps.en: Choose one thing in the classroom or the schoolyard to be your main thing, such as a plant, a chair, or a friend's backpack.
steps.zh: 在教室或校園裡選一樣東西當主角，例如一盆植物、一張椅子或同學的書包。

steps.en: Look at it through the window three ways: with the main thing in the middle, on a thirds point, and very close so that it fills the window.
steps.zh: 透過窗口用三種方式看它：主角在正中央、主角在三分點上、靠得很近讓主角塞滿窗口。

steps.en: Make a quick sketch of each one. Draw only the big shapes.
steps.zh: 每一種都畫一張快速的草圖，只畫大的形狀。

steps.en: Put a star next to the one you like best. Compare with a classmate who chose the same main thing.
steps.zh: 在你最喜歡的那一張旁邊畫一顆星。和選了同一個主角的同學比一比。

activities.tip_en: Moving the card closer to your eye shows more of the scene, and moving it away shows less, just like making the yellow frame bigger or smaller in Crop It.
activities.tip_zh: 卡紙拿近眼睛，看到的範圍變大；拿遠一點，範圍變小。這就像在「裁切看看」裡把黃色的框放大或縮小。

materials.en: White paper for the background
materials.zh: 一張白紙當底

materials.en: Light gray or pale paper and black paper
materials.zh: 淺灰或淡色的紙，和黑色的紙

materials.en: Scissors
materials.zh: 剪刀

steps.en: Cut one big circle from the pale paper and one small circle from the black paper.
steps.zh: 從淡色的紙剪一個大圓，從黑色的紙剪一個小圓。

steps.en: Lay them on the white paper, without glue, in three arrangements: both on one side, mirror-like if you can, and big near the middle with small far out.
steps.zh: 不用膠水，把它們放在白紙上，排出三種樣子：都放在同一邊；盡量左右對稱；大的靠近中間、小的放得很遠。

steps.en: For each one, ask three classmates whether it looks balanced. Write down their answers.
steps.zh: 每一種都問三位同學：看起來平衡嗎？把他們的回答寫下來。

steps.en: Copy each arrangement into the model on this page. Does the model agree with your classmates?
steps.zh: 把每一種擺法在這一頁的模型裡排一次。模型和同學的看法一樣嗎？

steps.en: Now hold the two paper circles in your hands. The black one is much lighter to hold, yet it may look heavier. Visual weight is not the weight of the paper.
steps.zh: 把兩個紙圓拿在手上。黑色的拿起來輕很多，看起來卻可能比較重。視覺重量不是紙的重量。

activities.tip_en: The screen shows gray by giving off light, and your paper shows it by reflecting the light in the room. Real paper may look a little different from the gray on the screen, so trust what you see on the desk.
activities.tip_zh: 螢幕上的灰色是螢幕自己發出的光，紙上的灰色是紙反射教室裡的光。真的紙看起來可能和螢幕上的灰不太一樣，請相信你在桌上看到的。

links_head.en: Near and far, the lens of a camera, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 遠和近、相機的鏡頭，以及下一課

links.note_zh: 重疊、大小和位置讓平面的畫看起來有深度；構圖則決定這些東西放在畫框裡的哪裡。

links.en: How Does a Camera Take a Picture?
links.note_en: Every photo has a frame too. That lesson explains how the lens makes the picture. This one is about what you put inside it.
links.note_zh: 每一張照片也都有邊框。那一課解釋鏡頭怎麼形成影像；這一課講你要把什麼放進框裡。

links.en: Why Do Drawn Faces Look Wrong?
links.zh: 為什麼畫的臉常常怪怪的？
links.note_en: Next comes proportion: where the eyes really are on a head, and why beginners often draw them too high.
links.note_zh: 下一課是比例：眼睛在頭上真正的位置，以及為什麼初學者常把眼睛畫得太高。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The balance point is computed by the page itself and covered by automatic tests; visual weight follows a simplified model of our own
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；重心由頁面自己計算，並有自動測試；視覺重量的算法是本教材自訂的簡化模型

sources.en: Balance as the distribution of visual weight; symmetrical, asymmetrical, and radial balance; emphasis; negative space has shape
sources.zh: 平衡是視覺重量的分配；對稱、不對稱、放射狀的平衡；強調；負空間有形狀
sources.src: J. Paul Getty Museum, Education, “Principles of Design” (worksheet)

sources.en: Composition is the arrangement of elements within a work of art
sources.zh: 構圖是作品裡各種元素的安排
sources.src: Tate, Art Term “Composition”

sources.en: Focal point, negative space, positive shapes, visual weight (usually from value or color contrast), rule of thirds as a general guideline
sources.zh: 焦點、負空間、正形、視覺重量（通常來自明暗或色彩的對比）、三分法是一般的參考原則
sources.src: Brigham Young University–Idaho, ART 110 glossary

sources.en: John Thomas Smith, Remarks on Rural Scenery (1797): the “Rule of thirds” applied to the sky in a landscape
sources.zh: 史密斯《鄉村風景評述》（1797）：把「三分法」用在風景畫的天空比例
sources.src: Internet Archive (scan of the 1797 book)

sources.en: A rule of thumb; first written down by Smith in 1797; George Field (1845): “neither accurate nor universal”
sources.zh: 經驗法則；1797 年由史密斯最早寫下；菲爾德（1845）：「既不精確，也不普遍」
sources.src: Wikipedia “Rule of thirds”

sources.en: The rule of thirds seems to play only a minor role, if any, in large sets of high-quality photographs and paintings
sources.zh: 在大量優秀的照片和畫作裡，三分法似乎只扮演很小的角色，甚至沒有
sources.src: Amirshahi et al., “Evaluating the Rule of Thirds in Photographs and Paintings,” Art & Perception 2 (2014): 163–182

sources.en: For a single object facing the viewer, preference was greatest at or near the center of the frame
sources.zh: 替一個正對觀眾的東西取景時，最受偏好的位置在畫框正中央或附近
sources.src: Palmer, Gardner & Wickens, Spatial Vision (2008), abstract on Europe PMC

sources.en: Gaze paths depend on the viewer's task; eyes and mouth in a face are looked at again and again
sources.zh: 目光的路線取決於看的人的任務；看臉時一再回到眼睛和嘴巴
sources.src: Wikipedia “Alfred L. Yarbus”

sources.en: In free viewing, people look at faces and text far more than at other regions of the same size and position
sources.zh: 自由觀看時，人看臉和文字的次數遠多於同樣大小、同樣位置的其他區域
sources.src: Cerf, Frady & Koch, Journal of Vision (2009), abstract on Europe PMC

sources.en: The Mona Lisa claim is not supported by Leonardo's writings; preference tests inconclusive at best
sources.zh: 〈蒙娜麗莎〉用黃金比例的說法在達文西的文字裡找不到根據；偏好的檢驗最多只能說沒有定論
sources.src: Wikipedia “Golden ratio”

sources.en: 計白當黑, 構圖 (Ministry of Education dictionary, via the Education Encyclopedia)
sources.zh: 「計白當黑」「構圖」（重編國語辭典修訂本）
sources.src: 教育百科〈計白當黑〉

sources.en: Standard Chinese terms: composition, focal point, emphasis, negative space, rule of thirds, cropping, formal and informal balance
sources.zh: 學術名詞：構圖、焦點、強調、負空間、三分構圖法、畫面剪裁、對稱均衡、非對稱均衡
sources.src: 國家教育研究院 樂詞網

sources.en: Learning content 視 E-Ⅲ-1, 視 A-Ⅲ-1; learning performance 2-Ⅲ-2, 視 1-Ⅳ-1
sources.zh: 學習內容：視 E-Ⅲ-1、視 A-Ⅲ-1；學習表現：2-Ⅲ-2、視 1-Ⅳ-1
sources.src: 十二年國教課綱 藝術領域（教育部，2018）
